summary: Sabetta International Airport serves the remote Yamal Peninsula community on the coast of the Ob Bay in northern Siberia, well above the Arctic Circle. It was developed primarily to support the Yamal LNG project and the adjacent Sabetta seaport, one of Russia's largest Arctic shipping terminals. The airport operates as a critical logistics hub for energy industry workers operating in one of the world's harshest climates.
faqs:
Q: Where is Sabetta International Airport located?
A: It is situated on the Yamal Peninsula in Russia's Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug, on the southeastern coast of the Ob Bay, approximately 71 degrees north latitude.

Q: What is the main purpose of Sabetta Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves the Yamal LNG project and the Sabetta seaport, providing passenger and cargo transport for energy industry personnel and operations in the Arctic region.

Q: When was Sabetta International Airport built?
A: The airport was constructed in the early 2010s to coincide with the development of the Yamal LNG facility and was opened to support the growing industrial activity in the region.

Q: Does the airport operate year-round in extreme Arctic conditions?
A: Yes, Sabetta Airport operates year-round despite extreme winter temperatures that can drop well below -40°C, with specialized equipment and procedures for polar operations.
transport_tips: Ground transport to and from Sabetta Airport is limited to official vehicle services, as the airport is located in a restricted industrial zone. Most travelers are transferred via pre-arranged transport linked to LNG project operations or charter services. There are no public buses or regular taxis serving the terminal, so visitors should confirm ground transportation in advance through their employer or sponsoring organization.
local_tip: Pack layered clothing even in summer — temperatures on the Yamal Peninsula can swing dramatically between cold mornings and relatively milder afternoons, and strong Arctic winds off the Ob Bay make it feel much colder than the thermometer suggests.
